displayName: ComputerEase by Deltek — job costing and accounting system for specialty/residential contractors
knownQuirks: **CE Live Service relay required for API access:** ComputerEase APIs are NOT directly internet-accessible. Deltek/ComputerEase exposes APIs via a 'CE Live Service' Windows service installed on the same VM as ComputerEase itself. External callers must hit a Deltek-managed URL, which routes the call back to the client's CE Live Service, which then proxies to the local ComputerEase instance. This is described by Deltek architects as a legacy relay pattern — 'a little bit different setup than how the modern APIs work'. Plan extra time for Deltek support tickets to configure this on the client VM. (Source: peerless transcript, 2026-04-17 — Raghuram Potluri.)

**Sandbox/practice environment has NO API access:** ComputerEase API Management menu is only available in the production environment. The practice (sandbox) environment does NOT expose API configuration. Attempts to access return 'Can't access API from practice'. Confirmed by Jean Jacobs (Peerless super-admin) on 2026-04-17. Implication: all API integration testing must occur in production with carefully scoped GET-only access groups until a separate Deltek-supported test path is negotiated. (Source: peerless transcript, 2026-04-17.)

**User creation requires PWMAINT system account:** New ComputerEase users cannot be created from a normal admin's session, even a super-admin. To create users you must log in as the PWMAINT account (password 'mp' historically) from the login screen, NOT from inside any menu. Jean Jacobs explicitly demonstrated this. Brian Cook: 'That's so weird that you have to log into a different account to create users.' Jean: 'It's a program that was DOS so who knows? Some of the stuff is still archaic.' (Source: peerless transcript, 2026-04-17.)

**Listening on port 445 (SMB), not 443 or 8081:** A `netstat`/listening-port check on a production ComputerEase VM showed it serving on TCP/445 only. Firewall rules for 443 and 8081 will not surface the ComputerEase service. The API exposure relies on the CE Live Service relay (see relay quirk above), so external integrations should target the Deltek-managed URL, NOT the customer VM directly on a standard HTTPS port. (Source: peerless transcript, 2026-04-16 — Brian Cook / Raghuram Potluri debugging.)

**Vendor support SLA tagged 'legacy' — 4-hour minimum response:** Deltek support categorises ComputerEase as a legacy product. Brian Cook: 'We're considered legacy. So, 4 hours, it won't be 2.' Plan client-side coordination accordingly — do not rely on same-hour Deltek support to unblock testing. (Source: peerless transcript, 2026-04-17.)

**Single super-admin is the norm — surface SPOF risk early:** ComputerEase deployments commonly have only ONE super-admin (the controller/accounting lead). At Peerless this person (Jean Jacobs) was on PTO and blocked all developer access for two days. Surface backup-admin question during scoping — do not assume IT has parity access. (Source: peerless transcript, 2026-04-15/16/17.)

**Sequential job-number policy:** Job numbers follow a sequential pattern by company code + product line + initials (e.g. '26 HD 565 AS' = year 26, Home Depot, sequence 565, initials AS). Test/dev work must NOT take the next sequential number — it will confuse live operators. Ashley Salerno explicitly avoided pulling the next-in-sequence number during demo to 'not confuse Mike while he's in here'. Integration writes must respect this gating. (Source: peerless transcript, 2026-04-16.)

**Standard objects to expose via API access group:** Confirmed Peerless API access group entitles: Jobs, Subcontracts, Cost Types, Job Totals, Service Work Orders. Excluded as PII/financial-sensitive: Payroll, Departments, Inventory items, Vendors. Default to GET-only on this object set during early integration; add write access per object only when business case is approved.

**Cameo is the UI access path, NOT the integration path:** Cameo (remote gateway product) is the recommended way to interactively log into ComputerEase — RDP guardrails are unknown. Cameo is NOT the integration channel for system-to-system flows; that channel is the CE Live Service relay URL. Do not confuse the two. (Source: peerless transcript, 2026-04-16 — Brian Cook.)
